Design
info:
A fairly common blog-style or content heavy
layout.

```
+-------------------------------------------+
| Title (h1)                                |
| Sub-title (div                            |
| Nav1 Nav2 Nav2 (menu)                     |
+-------------------------------------------+
+ Sidebar + Main (for articles)             |
| (aside) |                                 |
|         | +-----------------------------+ |
|         | | Article title (h2)          | |
|         | +-----------------------------+ |
|         | | Article body                | |
|         | +-----------------------------+ |
|         | +-----------------------------+ |
|         | | Article title (h2)          | |
|         | +-----------------------------+ |
|         | | Article body                | |
|         | +-----------------------------+ |
|         |                                 |
|         +---------------------------------+
|         | Footer                          |
+---------+---------------------------------+
```

Uses a CSS Grid with named grid template areas.
This makes it simple to adjust.

The areas for the layout above are:

```css
grid-template-areas: 
    "header header"
    "sidebar main"
    "sidebar footer";
```

To make the footer full width, use:

```css
grid-template-areas: 
    "header header"
    "sidebar main"
    "footer footer";
```

To move the sidebar to the right, use:

```css
grid-template-areas: 
    "header header"
    "main sidebar"
    "footer sidebar";
```

The example has a breakpoint for narrow
screens (set at 512px) where it switches to
a single column with the sidebar below the 
main area.

name: index.css
Markdown
Version: 2024-09-01
info:
This layout is designed to roughly replicate
the Node-RED Dashboard grid layout.

It keeps the outer layout from the content/blog
style (header, footer, left-sidebar, main).

But the sidebar now has the navigation menu
instead of the header.

The main content area is now a sub-grid. It has
the `id` of `more` which means that you can
easily add new content using uibuilder's 
no-code nodes.

Each `<article>` or `<div>` tag in the main 
content sub-grid can be considered the 
equivalent of a "widget" in Node-RED Dashboard 
terms. It can contain whatever you want it to.
It has a slightly different background colour
and a rounded border.

In the example all of the layout can be
controlled from the CSS variables in `:root`.

The sub-grid has 12 columns by default, you
can change that to whatever is useful to you.

The articles have a default width of 3. You can
easily override a single article by adding:
`--article-width: 6` or however many columns
you want it to take up.

By default, specific grid rows are undefined
(set to `auto`) so articles take up whatever
height they need. If you want to define the
rows, you can easily do so by changing
`--main-rows` to `repeat(12, 1fr)` or some
other number. You have lots of control over the
column/row layout but it can get a bit complex
so you are advised to keep it simple, at least
to start with.

-----------------

## NOTES

It is very likely that much of the
defined CSS in this example will be incorporated
into UIBUILDER's `uib-brand.css` in the 
future.

The Markdown-IT library has been included in
`index.html`, loaded from a public Internet
CDN. Install & use the library locally using 
UIBUILDER's library manager if you prefer.
Or remove completely if you don't need to use
Markdown dynamic content.

name: uibuilder standard output
info:
This shows the data coming out of the
uibuilder node's Port #1 (top) which is
the standard output.

Here you will see any standard msg sent from
your front-end code.

name: uibuilder control output
info:
This shows the data coming out of the
uibuilder node's Port #2 (bottom) which is
the control output.

Here you will see any control msg either sent
by the node itself or from the front-end library.

For example the "client disconnect" and
"client connect" messages. Or the "visibility"
messages from the client.

Loop the "client connect", "cache replay" and
"cache clear" messages back to a `uib-cache`
node before the input to uibuilder in order
to control the output of the cache.

info:
CSS Selectors can be used in different ways. In this case
you can use either of:

```css
#eltest-tbl-table > tbody > tr.r2 > td.r2.c2
```
or
```css
#eltest-tbl tbody:nth-child(2) > tr:nth-child(2) > td:nth-child(2)
```

However, using the `r2`, `c2` class names can be 
fragile if dynamically changing the size of the 
table because those class names are not updated
automatically.

Get CSS Selector ideas from your browsers dev tools.

Test selectors using the `$('...')` helper function
in the dev tools console. e.g.

```js
$('#eltest-tbl-table > tbody > tr.r2 > td.r2.c2')
```
